summary: Practise Windows, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, email, and online safety in an ICDL-aligned computer literacy course. Explore the course.
lede: Computer literacy training helps office staff, entry-level professionals, and career changers handle routine digital work. You practise organizing files, creating and formatting documents, using spreadsheet formulas and charts, and preparing presentations, while building safe email, online research, and account habits. It also introduces ICDL skill areas and AI-assisted office features at overview level.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for people building the computer and productivity-software skills needed to complete routine office work, support colleagues, and prepare clear digital outputs. This course is designed for: Office administrators organizing shared folders and preparing routine correspondence. Administrative assistants formatting Word documents and maintaining digital records. Entry-level professionals creating spreadsheets, presentations, and workplace communications. Career changers building foundational computer skills for office-based roles. Reception and front-desk staff managing email, attachments, and digital schedules. Junior accounts clerks entering figures and checking basic Excel calculations. Human resources assistants formatting staff documents and organizing electronic files. Sales support coordinators updating spreadsheets and preparing presentation materials. Customer service representatives using email and online resources for case responses. Team coordinators sharing files and maintaining consistent office document practices.
modules: ICDL Digital Safety and Skills Plan
prerequisites: Designed for entry-level learners; no prior productivity-software experience is assumed. No coding or programming is required. For hands-on practice, access to a Windows computer and the listed office applications is recommended; software access and device arrangements should be confirmed before delivery.
